title: Nose & Olfactory System
shortDescription: The nasal structures involved in smell, and the basic pathway from odor molecule to brain.
genZNote: Helps you smell — a short pathway most people never think about until it's blocked.

structures.name: Nasal cavity
structures.description: The main air space inside the nose.
structures.function: Warms, humidifies, and filters incoming air; houses olfactory receptors.

structures.name: Nasal conchae (turbinates)
structures.description: Curved bony shelves inside the nasal cavity.
structures.function: Increase surface area to warm, humidify, and filter air.

structures.name: Olfactory bulb
structures.description: Structure at the base of the brain, above the nasal cavity.
structures.function: Receives signals from olfactory nerves and relays them for processing.

structures.name: Olfactory nerves
structures.description: Nerve fibers running from receptors in the nasal cavity to the olfactory bulb.
structures.function: Carry smell signals to the brain.

steps: Odor molecules enter the nasal cavity

questions.prompt: Which structures increase the nasal cavity's surface area to warm and filter air?
questions.explanation: The nasal conchae (turbinates) are curved bony shelves that increase surface area for warming, humidifying, and filtering air.
optionNotes: Processes smell signals, not airflow surface area.
Carries smell signals, doesn't affect airflow surface area.
Part of the ear, unrelated to the nose.

questions.prompt: In the labelled nose illustration, which structure directly receives signals from the olfactory nerves?
questions.explanation: The olfactory bulb receives signals from the olfactory nerves and relays them toward the brain for processing.
optionNotes: The space where odor molecules first enter, not the receiving structure.
Increases surface area, doesn't receive nerve signals directly.
Part of the throat, unrelated to olfactory signaling.

sections.heading: Structures
bullets: Nasal cavity — the main air-filled space behind the nose.
Nasal conchae (turbinates) — ridged structures that increase surface area to warm, humidify, and filter incoming air.
Olfactory bulb — sits at the base of the brain, just above the nasal cavity; the first relay point for smell signals.
Olfactory nerves — carry smell signals from receptors in the nasal cavity to the olfactory bulb.

sections.heading: Basic Smell Pathway
sections.body: Odor molecules enter the nasal cavity → bind to olfactory receptors → olfactory nerves carry the signal → olfactory bulb relays it → the brain interprets the signal as a specific smell.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The olfactory system detects airborne odor molecules in the nasal cavity and relays that information via the olfactory nerves and bulb to the brain.
keyFacts: Nasal conchae increase surface area to warm, filter, and humidify air.
The olfactory bulb is the first brain structure to receive smell signals.
Smell receptors sit in the lining of the nasal cavity.
commonConfusion: Nasal conchae (air conditioning of incoming air) is sometimes confused with the olfactory receptors themselves (smell detection) — they serve different roles in the same cavity.

highYieldFacts: The olfactory bulb sits directly above the nasal cavity, close to the brain — one reason smell is so closely linked to memory and emotion.
commonTraps: Don't confuse the nasal conchae's air-conditioning role with the actual smell-detection role of olfactory receptors.
mustRemember: Pathway: odor molecules → nasal cavity receptors → olfactory nerves → olfactory bulb → brain.
